posts.text: The Big Ten now owns college sports. Three straight college football titles and the trifecta this year: a football title and men’s and women’s titles too. This is the first Big Ten men’s title since 2000, it has been a long time in the title wilderness.

Chicago is more dangerous to Americans than Iran is. And if you didn’t say a word about the 25th amendment when Joe Biden was in office don’t you dare mention it for Trump. I discussed with @JesseBWatters.

Video

Prediction markets in sports vs sports books, is it a distinction without a legal difference? What will the courts say and will the Supreme Court ultimately decide the issue? A deep dive with @ChairmanSelig. Legal nerds will enjoy this.


The Clay Travis & Buck Sexton Show (@clayandbuck)

Bonus Content: @ClayTravis  and CFTC @ChairmanSelig nerd out over prediction markets, sports and more!

Dan Hurley is the best coach in college basketball, but Michigan wins by double digits tonight. Wolverines are just too good.

Video
nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1jGXgeDna…

UNC now has pro champion coaches for its top college programs: Belichick and now Malone.


Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel)

Sources: North Carolina intends to hire longtime NBA coach Michael Malone as the school’s next basketball coach. He’s an NBA Championship coach with the Denver Nuggets from the 2022-23 season and has won 510 games as an NBA head coach.





— https://nitter.net/PeteThamel/status/2041212222462910658#m

Third circuit rules prediction markets can feature sports contracts and that federal law via CFTC supersedes state gambling law. Big battle here over whether state of New Jersey could shut down prediction markets. Likely headed to Supreme Court: courtlistener.com/docket/703…

Megan Rapinoe says the Olympics requiring women’s sports to be played by women is “hateful” and has no basis in science. Sue Bird agrees. Retired women’s athletes supporting their own erasure from sports is wild to see.

Video
BTW, here’s what my Twitter data board shows for the first three months of the year. No idea how this compares to other accounts above. But just for full disclosure.
I also later lost $50k selling khaki pants in college colors. I still think this was a brilliant idea. outkick.com/analysis/how-i-l…

I didn’t watch the NCAA women’s tournament, but it ending with everyone hating Geno Auriemma and then Dawn Staley’s team losing by 30 in the title game feels like the perfect conclusion. Well done, ladies.

Khakis were so popular the biggest debate turned into pleated vs plain front. Pleated was for losers. (There was also a brief corduroy fad in here too. I know because I folded and rolled all these pants at American Eagle and Abercrombie from 1995 to 2000).

This was the peak of the khaki pants era, when it seemed jeans were forever dead. From like 1992 to 2000, khakis dominated. I don’t think I even owned a pair of jeans then.


Jeff Eisenberg (@JeffEisenberg)

This was Dusty May's first Final Four in Indianapolis. He and three other Indiana student managers posted up in the lobby of the downtown Marriott to "hopefully bump into any coach" and "try to beg" for a spot on their staff.





— https://nitter.net/JeffEisenberg/status/2040936541678100773

No idea how this is measured, but thanks for all the engagement, guys. I’m in the top right here. And for better or worse, every Tweet on here is written by me.


Nate Silver (@NateSilver538)

These are the Twitter/X accounts with the most engagement so far in 2026. I suppose I had some intuition for how bad it was, but jeez, this is what you get when the ecosystem is broken.





— https://nitter.net/NateSilver538/status/2040909183525048638#m
